title: I Let the Study-Group Shared Notes Policy Catch the Person Who Sold Them

parts.text: I opened Discord at 11:40 p.m. and found our midterm notes listed on a campus marketplace for twelve dollars. The study-group rule we voted on said notes stay in the channel. I was twenty-one, bio major, holding a laptop and a highlighter hangover. The seller photo cropped our header but left my unique typo: mitocondria, which I had refused to fix as a watermark. I archived the listing, the typo, and the vote screenshot. Then I posted both in the channel without a name. At 11:48 Kyle typed lol wild and changed his marketplace handle.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Kyle just changed the handle; the listing still has my watermark typo.

social.video_title: Twelve-dollar notes with my mitocondria watermark — Part 1/2
social.description: Discord vote, marketplace, a typo I kept. The handle changed. Would you have named him?

parts.text: The TA already had the honor-code inbox. I forwarded the archive as a packet, not a rant. Kyle got a zero on the group portion and had to write a reflection that used correctly spelled mitochondria. The listing died. We voted a new rule: watermarks stay. I fixed the typo in the real notes. Twelve dollars is not a study group. Discord stayed boring, which is the point of notes.

social.video_title: He had to spell mitochondria in a reflection — Part 2/2
social.description: Honor code packet, group zero, fixed notes. Was a marketplace a channel?
